moral.zh: 捂住自己的耳朵，改变不了真实发生的事。做错了要诚实面对，及时改正。
moral.en: Hiding the truth from yourself does not change it. Face mistakes honestly and make them right.

idiomMeaning.zh: 比喻自己欺骗自己，以为看不见、听不见，事情就不存在。古文写的是盗钟，后来演化为“掩耳盗铃”。
idiomMeaning.en: Literally, covering one’s ears while stealing a bell; it means fooling yourself into believing a problem is gone simply because you ignore it. The classical source tells of a large bronze bell.

pages.zh: 从前，有个人路过一座古宅，看见院里挂着一口漂亮的大钟。
pages.en: Long ago, a man passed an old courtyard and spotted a beautiful bronze bell inside.

pages.zh: 他想偷偷搬走大钟，可钟又大又重，怎么也抬不动。
pages.en: He tried to sneak the bell away, but it was far too big and heavy to lift.

pages.zh: 他想：“用木槌把钟敲开，不就能一块块带走了吗？”
pages.en: Then he thought, “If I break it into pieces, I can carry it away bit by bit.”

pages.zh: 木槌刚碰到大钟，响亮的钟声就一下传遍了村子。
pages.en: The instant the mallet touched the bell, a great ringing sound rolled across the village.

pages.zh: 他赶紧捂住自己的耳朵，又敲了一下，心想：“这回没人听见了！”
pages.en: He covered his own ears and tapped again, thinking, “Now no one can hear it!”

pages.zh: 可是，村民们听得清清楚楚，纷纷循着钟声来到院门口。
pages.en: But the villagers heard every ring and followed the sound straight to the courtyard gate.

pages.zh: 老人说：“你听不见，别人却听得见。这就是掩耳盗铃呀！”
pages.en: The keeper said, “You may block your own ears, but everyone else can still hear. That is covering your ears while stealing a bell!”

pages.zh: 他红着脸道了歉，把钟留在原处。从此，他不再用假装来逃避真相。
pages.en: He apologized and left the bell where it belonged. From then on, he stopped pretending that problems disappeared when ignored.
